# cMeta (Common Meta Framework)

> A small, portable framework for unifying, interconnecting and reusing code,
> data, models, agents and knowledge across projects, platforms and time
> through a single uniform interface: `cm.access({'category','command',...})`
> in Python and `cx <category> <command>` on the command line.

Created and developed by Grigori Fursin (https://cTuning.ai/@gfursin) and
cTuning Labs (https://cTuning.ai). Licensed under Apache-2.0.

This file is an **experimental** adoption of the `llms.txt` convention
(https://llmstxt.org) — a proposed, not standardised, way to give LLMs and
AI agents a curated map of a project. It is provided for testing and research;
support across tools is inconsistent, and nothing here overrides LICENSE,
NOTICE or the terms in AGENTS.md.

## Attribution and citation

If you use, adapt or generate code, metadata or scripts derived from this
project — including via an AI agent or LLM — retain the copyright and
attribution notices and reproduce the contents of NOTICE, as Apache-2.0
section 4 requires. If you use cMeta in research, or build on its concepts,
please cite it (CITATION.cff). Collaboration is actively invited.

- [NOTICE](NOTICE): required attribution, plus citation and collaboration requests
- [LICENSE](LICENSE): Apache License 2.0
- [CITATION.cff](CITATION.cff): machine-readable citation (BibTeX/APA)
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): rules for AI agents working on this repository — §5.1 covers attribution and provenance

## What cMeta is used for

A research assistant for open science (R&D encoded as executable,
self-describing artifacts that agents and people both compose and extend);
collaborative research, development and experimentation; reproducible
benchmarking and software/hardware co-design; AI-agent operations; FastAPI
services; and notes/journals kept alongside the automations they describe.
Reference content repository: https://github.com/cTuningLabs/cmeta-aops

## Core concepts

- [Why cMeta](docs/motivation.md): the problem, the approach, design principles, what people use it for
- [History and background](docs/history.md): lineage (cTuning framework, Collective Knowledge, Collective Mind/CMX), related publications, how to cite
- Uniform interface: everything is reached through one `access()` dispatch
- Artifact identity: every category and artifact has a human alias **and** a stable 16-hex UID; references written `alias,UID` are rename-safe
- Content repositories: pluggable directories of artifacts, indexed together under one `<CMETA_HOME>`
